question.text: This politician and general opposed the Vichy government, instead leading Free France during World War II. He later established the Fifth Republic in France.
question.answerHtml: Charles de Gaulle (accept Charles Andr´e Joseph Marie de Gaulle)
question.clue: This man answered "no" in response to the questions "must hope disappear? Is defeat final?" in his Appeal of June 18th speech.

swap.leadin: Name these regions or cities that are famous for their iconic foods.
swap.text: This region in France produces a bubbly wine that is commonly used during celebrations.
swap.clue: Breaking from the trend in the 19th century for wines from this region to be sweet, producer Perrier-Jouet produced a dry wine that critics called brut ("brute") for its perceived severity.

question.text: This leader of the Second French Empire was captured by the Prussians at the Battle of Sedan. He shares his name with his uncle, an earlier French emperor.
question.clue: This ruler also militarily supported the claim of Maximilian I to the Mexican throne, until the ultimate defeat of monarchist and French forces at the 1862 Battle of Puebla.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the French Revolution.
swap.text: After being deposed by revolutionaries, Louis was moved from his Palace at Versailles to what other palace located on the banks of the Seine River?
swap.clue: Following the march on Versailles, Louis XVI was forced to live in this palace in France, originally commissioned by Catherine de' Medici. This palace later served as Napoleon's imperial palace.

question.text: While the plague was going on, Edward III decided to claim the French throne, sparking this conflict. Philip VI's fleet was defeated at the Bay of Sluys during this conflict.
question.clue: A nine-year reprieve from this conflict was secured with the Treaty of Bretigny, and the failure of Genoese crossbows allowed one commander to "earn his spurs" in its battle of Crecy.

swap.leadin: William Longsword succeeded a duke of this region who acquired it in the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte (SAH-klair-soor-EP-tuh).
swap.text: Name this region, now in northern France, whose first Scandinavian duke took control here 175 years before a descendant commissioned the Domesday (dooms-day) Book.
swap.clue: The second ranger battalion climbed up the Pointe du Hoc during this action.

question.leadin: It began on August 23, 1572 in Paris.
question.text: Name this event, which saw the Admiral de Coligny and thousands of others of his religious beliefs killed.
question.clue: This event was precipitated by the wedding of Margaret of Valois.

swap.text: This battle, with the objective of "bleeding France white," was fought on the river Meuse. Philippe Petain was hailed as the savior of this battle where Robert Nivelle proclaimed "they shall not pass."
swap.clue: Before advancing, the attacking side in this battle undertook a 10-hour bombardment, during which they fired one million shells.

question.text: In this 1805 victory, Napoleon crushed a combined Russian and Austrian army of nearly 85,000 men. Soon after, he was able to capture Vienna.
question.clue: Sokolnitz changed hands several times during this battle, and prior to its start, General Kutuzov was demoted.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about incidents in which Jews have been expelled from a country.
swap.text: All Jews were expelled from France by this monarch prior to the launching of the Seventh Crusade. This son of Blanche of Castile constructed the Sainte-Chapelle to house a piece of the True Cross.
swap.clue: This man's exploits were chronicled by Jean de Joinville.

question.leadin: Lines of fortification were popular during the Second World War.
question.text: Named for a French war hero and minister of war, it stretched from the Italian border to , but still didn't prevent Hitler from advancing through the and invading.
question.clue: Army Group C conducted a holding action at this place, which allowed Army Groups A and B to move north and then west in the sickle-slice maneuver.

swap.leadin: It is said that St. Anselm elected not to join its namesake monastic congregation when he realized how little time would be left for his personal study.
swap.text: Identify this congregation, named for an abbey, which was founded in 909 when William the Pious gave his Burgundian hunting grounds to the Church and first led by abbot Berno of Baume.
swap.clue: Cardinals Richelieu and Mazarin both led this institution while serving as ministers to the kings of France.

question.leadin: The Legion of Marat was created to police anti-revolutionaries in this city during the War in the Vendee ("von-DAY").
question.text: Name this city in which mass drownings were carried about via "republican marriages" in which men and women were tied together and drowned. The Peace of Alais ("ah-LESS"), signed shortly after the 1627 Siege of La Rochelle, altered a law named for this city.
question.clue: A series of massacres took place in this city in 1793 when priests were loaded into (+) barges that were then intentionally sunk.

swap.leadin: This man gained a fiefdom from King Charles the Simple with the signing of the Treaty of Saint Clair-sur-Epte.
swap.text: Name this father of William Longsword and wife of either Poppa or Gisela. His conversion to Christianity gave him control of a certain French region, though by the time he died, he had to massacre a hundred Christian prisoners to keep himself sane.
swap.clue: In some sources this man was known as 'Ganger' or 'walker' because he was too large to mount a horse, and he is said to be the son of the earl of More, while the more dubious Dudo of St. Quentin claims that he came from 'Dacia', probably indicating Denmark.

question.leadin: Answer the following on the career of Joseph Gallieni.
question.text: In Madagascar, Gallieni commanded this officer who later served ahead of Gallieni as Commander-in-Chief of French Forces on the Western Front until 1916.
question.clue: This incompetent general was the Commander in Chief of French forces at the beginning of World War I. He adopted the disastrous Plan XVII [pron. "17"] but managed to recover from initial defeats to check the German advance at the Battle of the Marne.

swap.text: During this event, Stephen of Cloyes went to Saint-Denis to deliver a letter from Jesus to Philip II. The participants in this event led by Nicholas of Cologne were supposedly sold into slavery in Tunisia.
swap.clue: Nicholas of Cologne's prediction that the sea by Genoa would part for this campaign obviously did not come true, and when this crusade ended, most of its participants were sold into slavery.

question.leadin: Name these advisors to French kings.
question.text: This Protestant was a chief advisor to Henry IV. Apart from encouraging agriculture and building roads, he is famous for fighting corruption in tax collection, leading to a massive increase in government revenue.
question.answer: Maximilien de Bethune, duc de Sully

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a French statesman.
swap.text: Earlier Thiers had served in various ministerial posts under this French monarch who replaced Charles X in the July Revolution.
swap.clue: This ruler was caricatured as Gargantua in a lithograph by Honore Daumier ("ON-o-ray daw-mya").

question.text: The father of all commentary on Lamentations, as with the Tanach as a whole, is this 11th and 12th Century French Rabbi.

swap.text: During the 15th century Brittany was ruled by two dukes of this name. The second duke of this name teamed up with Charles the Bold to fight the War of the League of the Public Weal and tried to invade England.
swap.clue: Before becoming king, the second French monarch of this name became King Consort of Scotland by marrying Mary, Queen of Scots.
